# Ida Ashdown

## Overview

- **Age:** 10  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034)</sub>
- **Origin:** Juneford  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Ida lacks conventional beauty but is considered endearing. She has slanted, deep-blue eyes, minute ivory teeth, and plaits of limp, pitch-black hair that she brushes to a satiny smoothness. She often wears faded clothing, including an ill-fitting jacket and a discolored tam.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c18 P8](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0008), [v5 c34 P5](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0005)_

## Personality

Ida is a timid, quiet, and sensitive girl who detests conflict and is deeply touchy regarding the opinions of others. Compassionate and gentle-hearted, she feels profound sympathy for others and enjoys prayer. Despite her extreme shyness, she acts bravely when driven by love for her family.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c5 P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 c9 P10](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0010), [v5 c17 P23](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0023), [v5 c23 P16](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0016), [v5 c31 P13](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0013), [v5 c34 P13](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0013), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)_

## History

Ida moved with her family from Juneford to Glen St. Agnes. Having lost her mother at age six, she frequently felt jealous of children with living mothers while cherishing memories of her own. When Mary Stubbs took shelter at the parsonage, Ida showed her great compassion, helped prepare a bed for her in the garret, and learned how to clean plates from her. After Elder Baxter altered the prayer-meeting schedule, Ida and Grace accidentally confused the days of the week, causing them to miss Sunday School and perform household cleaning on Sunday instead. When Mrs. Twiss attempted to adopt Ida under the impression that her father neglected her, Mr. Ashdown refused. During the Good-Conduct Club's self-imposed discipline, Ida fainted from fasting, causing her father intense distress. Following Mary's warnings about stepmothers, Ida worried about her father marrying again; however, after overhearing her father's solitary anguish, she bravely visited Clementine Ainslie to ask her to marry him to make him happy.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P26](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0026), [v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 c5 P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 c5 P93](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0093), [v5 c10 P21](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0021), [v5 c12 P6](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0006), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c14 P36](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0036), [v5 c23 P82](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0082), [v5 c28 P13](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0013), [v5 c33 P36](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0036), [v5 c34 P13](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0013), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)_
